Let's be blunt: Timius's stats are showing their age.

In an era where modern attackers boast 1300+ base attack, Timius sits significantly lower. This is critical because his special skill damage scales directly off the difference between his Attack and the enemy's Defense.
By modern standards, he is squishy. Modern tank busters and snipers can often one-shot or severely cripple him before he fires.
He has fallen from "Tank/Flank material" to "Protected Wing" or "Offense-Only Specialist." He requires Limit Break 2 (LB2) and full emblems just to survive the opening volley of a modern match.

Upon release, Timius was an absolute beast. He was the "Fortuna killer" and a nightmare for Holy tanks like Shaal or Erlang Shen. His ability to strip buffs at Fast speed made him a staple in top-tier defenses.

The "Moonrise" mechanic is his Achilles' heel in the long run. Since damage scales off raw stats, and his stats are frozen in 2023 while enemies get stronger in 2026, his damage potential has plummeted. He simply cannot overcome the Defense stats of modern heroes to deal his maximum damage without significant external help (Growth/Wither).
You don't bring him for the damage anymore. You bring him because you need a Fast Dispel + Buff Block to counter a specific threat (like a Taunt hero). He is a tactical tool, not a nuker.

If you pull Timius early, he is a godsend. His Dispel/Block combo will carry you through almost all map stages, raids, and early wars. Prioritize leveling him as your main Blue hero.

He is a luxury tool. Do not prioritize his LB2 unless you lack a modern Dispel/Blocker. He is useful for depth in War teams, specifically to counter Taunt or heavy buff teams, but he should not be your primary damage dealer. Treat him as a support hero who happens to do some chip damage.
When Timius released, many players felt "SG is seriously MEAN" because he instantly made heroes like Fortuna feel obsolete due to his Dispel-first mechanic.
The community spent weeks trying to decipher the damage formula. As one player noted, "It’s a match-3 game, why do I need a PhD in math to know how much damage I'll do?"
Players quickly noted his specific malice towards Yellow heroes, with one user calling him a "Holy Hater" that makes Yellow tanks regret their life choices.
